title: Embeddings and vector search
hook: Exact, keyword, vector and hybrid search, and where to keep the vectors.
inPlainWords: An embedding turns text, an image, or a product into a list of numbers so that similar meanings land close together. Vector search finds the closest ones. It finds meaning, not exact words.

useCase.title: Let customers search for "something warm for a windy hike"
useCase.story: ShopEase has 50,000 products. Customers type natural phrases, not product names. Search must also handle exact codes like XR-2040-B.

approaches.name: Keyword search
approaches.what: Match words and their close forms, ranked by how rare and relevant they are.
approaches.avoidWhen: Different words that mean the same thing.

approaches.name: Vector (semantic) search
approaches.what: Embed the query and the products, then return the nearest by meaning.
approaches.greatWhen: Natural phrases, synonyms and several languages.
approaches.example: "Warm for a windy hike" finds insulated windproof jackets.

approaches.name: Hybrid search
approaches.what: Run keyword and vector search together and merge the results.
approaches.greatWhen: Real catalogs with both codes and phrases.
approaches.example: Codes are found by keyword and intent by vector.

approaches.name: Where to keep the vectors
approaches.what: A vector index inside your existing database, or a dedicated vector store.
approaches.greatWhen: Inside your database means fewer moving parts. A dedicated store suits huge scale.
approaches.avoidWhen: A separate store as the only copy of the data.
approaches.example: Product embeddings sitting next to the product table.

approaches.name: Choosing and refreshing embeddings
approaches.what: Pick an embedding model, and re-embed when the model or the data changes.
approaches.avoidWhen: Mixing vectors from different models in one index.

challenge.question: Customers type "something warm for a windy hike", and also exact codes like XR-2040-B. What search setup fits?

options.text: Hybrid: vector for meaning, keyword for codes, with filters like in-stock
options.why: Each method covers the other's weakness.
Great for codes, but it misses "windbreaker" for "windy".
Understands phrases, but may return look-alike codes.
Nobody types a product's exact name for a vague need.

bestCase.title: Hybrid search with filters, and a plan for refreshing embeddings
bestCase.example: "Something warm for a windy hike" finds insulated windproof jackets by meaning. "XR-2040-B" is found by keyword. Filters hide out-of-stock items. New products are embedded overnight, so search stays fresh.

worstCase.title: Vector-only, mixed models and stale vectors
worstCase.example: A search for XR-2040-B returns similar-looking codes. Half the catalog was embedded with an old model and half with a new one, so distances mean nothing. New products never appear because nobody re-embedded them.

route.travelling: Query: "something warm for a windy hike"

steps.label: Embedding model
steps.goes: One model turns every product into a list of numbers.
steps.goesWrong: Half the catalog was embedded with an old model and half with a new one.

steps.label: Two indexes
steps.goes: A vector index and a keyword index, with metadata like stock and price.

steps.label: Customer query
steps.goes: The customer types a natural phrase.

steps.label: Embed the query
steps.goes: It is turned into numbers with the same model.

steps.label: Search both ways
steps.goes: Vector finds meaning. Keyword finds codes.

steps.label: Merge and filter
steps.goes: Results are combined and out-of-stock items are hidden.

takeaway: Embeddings find meaning, keywords find exact words and codes. Real search uses both, with one embedding model kept up to date.
